newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.8 pct in March - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.8 pct in March - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.8 percent in the second week of fiscal March versus February, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.
The index rose 8.3 percent compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 8.0 percent in the week ended March 15 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.

The figures this week were a moderate retreat from last week due to colder weather coupled with tougher comparisons against high sales levels in the second week of March last year, said Howard Eilenberg, retail analyst at Redbook Research.

"(Retailers) are up against a very strong week a year ago ... and weather turned a bit colder, so the sales of spring goods may have slowed down a bit," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
"I think it was just a modest blip," he said, adding that, on a month-to-date basis, stores are still ahead of their plan.
Eilenberg said retailers are still optimistic for the month and sales performance so far this year has been very strong.
Higher-priced apparel continued to lead sales growth at department stores, he said.
In merchandise categories, discount stores reported strength in hard line goods, such as high-markup gardening equipment and supplies, small appliances and housewares, and children's apparel.
Looking forward, Eilenberg said retailers should experience strong business over the next two weeks because of the Easter holiday.
"Look at the month as a whole ... that will be a little better than expected," Eilenberg added.
